terms.definition: The exposed core of a dead Sun-like star: about the size of Earth, holding up to 1.4 solar masses, shining only from leftover heat.
terms.function: The final stage for most stars, including the Sun.

terms.definition: The pressure that arises because electrons refuse to be squeezed into the same space — it holds a white dwarf up even though nothing is burning.
terms.whyItMatters: It proves support does not need fire.

terms.definition: The glowing shell of gas a red giant puffs off before the white dwarf is exposed — named centuries ago for its planet-like roundness.
terms.function: Recycles star matter back into the galaxy, enriching the next star generation.
terms.whyItMatters: Most of the elements beyond hydrogen and helium reach new stars this way.

terms.definition: The maximum mass of a white dwarf, about 1.4 solar masses; beyond it electron pressure can no longer prevent collapse.
terms.function: Sets the threshold where a remnant must become a neutron star or explode.

terms.definition: Matter packed so tightly that quantum effects, not heat, create its pressure — the substance a white dwarf is made of.
terms.whereItIs: The whole interior of the dwarf
terms.whyItMatters: One teaspoon of it weighs about 5.5 tons.
